shortened: This servant of Thine believed in the Word of Thy mercy and turned toward the Kingdom of Thy oneness and was attracted by the verses of Thy holiness and was set ablaze by the fire kindled in the Tree of Thy unity and heard Thy call and responded to Thy summons and bore every hardship and trial in Thy path. Then he ascended unto Thee and rose to the seat of truth in Thy Kingdom.

order.why: Read a life of guiding others within a plea for cleansing.
shortened: My God, my God! This is Thy servant who heard Thy call and responded to Thy summons, who turned toward Thee and spoke in praise of Thee, who called the people to the kingdom of Thy oneness and guided them to the heaven of Thy singleness, who gave glad tidings of the manifestation of the signs of Thy sanctification among the righteous and attracted them to the kingdom of mysteries, and who remained firm in Thy religion until he returned unto Thee, placing his trust in Thee.
O Lord! Cleanse him from the stain of disobedience and cause him to enter the kingdom of forgiveness.

order.why: Consider active service continuing beyond the world of dust.
Read revived spirit and a truthful tongue among later generations.
shortened: Prayer:
O my God! O my God! This is Thy servant, associated with the Beloved Leader of the Messengers at Thy holy threshold among all worlds.

O Lord, assist him with Thy confirmations and revive his spirit with Thy breaths and cause him to ascend to the kingdom of Thy verses and admit him into the gardens of Thy pardon and forgiveness, and give him a truthful tongue among those who come after.

order.why: Preserve the distinct petitions for an extended circle of souls.
Keep the named requests for shelter, dwelling and absolution.
shortened: O Lord! Shelter Nushiravan in the refuge of Thy mercy, and grant Isfandiyar Mihraban a dwelling place in the Garden of Paradise and the heavenly Paradise. Forgive and pardon Firuz Javanmard, and grant absolution to Siyyid Husayn Mirza Ja'far in the presence of Thy great mercy.

order.why: Remember Nazim’s forgiveness and kindness to enemies.
shortened: Verily Your servant Nazim was one who suppressed anger and forgave sins and harm, showing kindness to enemies even if they were the most bitter foes, thirsting for the fountainhead of guidance, yearning to attain the Supreme Concourse, and eagerly anticipating the appointed time until his desire was fulfilled and his destiny arrived, and he drank the cup of death and soared like a dove to the flying place of the birds of immortality.

order.why: Consider earthly service as sowing for a later harvest.
Read the two bright candles through their service to humanity.
shortened: O Merciful Lord! These two blessed souls were two bright candles who rendered service to the human world.
May all-encompassing forgiveness be granted and everlasting life be realized.

order.why: Close the linked readings with survivors continuing a loved one’s good example.
shortened: Grant the wishes of her heart and soul and make her survivors firm and steadfast in the right way and in the Path of the Kingdom, so that they may light the lamp of that attracted one, and walk in her footsteps. May her descendants be related to Thy threshold in this world and may they be known in the Name.

order.why: Retain the supplied prayer’s welcome of poor, stranger and thirsty soul.
End with the supplied remembrance of a life of reflection and devotion.

questions: How do these passages make room for both grief and hope? Which words or images help you attend compassionately to someone who is mourning?
What might it mean to pray for another while acknowledging one’s own need for forgiveness? How does that humility shape the breadth of intercession?
How do the images of a guest, a bird, a garden, and a new beginning illuminate the hopes expressed for the departed?
What relationships between the living and the departed emerge in the prayers for parents, children, companions, and communities?
What affinities and differences do you notice between the comparative readings and these prayers, especially concerning mercy, forgiveness, and continued relationship?
How could charitable action or continuing a loved one’s good example become part of remembrance? Which connected subject would deepen that exploration?

references.label: 1 · 2 Maccabees 12:38–46 · Prayer and hope for the departed
references.note: After the recovery of fallen soldiers, the narrative describes prayer concerning their wrongdoing and an offering made with resurrection in view. Read this account in its own historical and sacrificial setting beside the compilation’s prayers for forgiveness. Compare the hopes that make intercession meaningful while attending to the distinct theological accounts.

references.label: 2 · Qur’an 59:10 · Remembering those who preceded us
references.note: The speakers ask forgiveness for themselves and earlier believers, together with freedom from rancor toward fellow believers. The verse concerns those who preceded them in faith without explicitly identifying every predecessor as deceased. Compare its joined concern for others and for the praying heart with the compilation’s inclusive petitions for mercy.
